subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add a core browser SSRF private-network approval policy, and what first-phase shape is acceptable?
rationale: The request changes browser egress security semantics, public config, and possibly CLI/UI approval flows; automation cannot choose those product and security tradeoffs safely.

options.title: Approve staged browser policy
options.body: Start with a narrow browser-owned allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata/link-local semantics, then add interactive confirmation only after prompt, timeout, rate-limit, and session-state UX is specified.

options.title: Keep existing strict knobs
options.body: Leave the current deny, broad opt-in, and hostname exception model in place and document why interactive private-network grants are unsupported.

options.title: Fold into broader egress design
options.body: Resolve this with the related browser denylist and web_fetch private-network policy work before adding browser-specific config.

recommendation.title: Approve staged browser policy
recommendation.body: Start with a narrow browser-owned allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata/link-local semantics, then add interactive confirmation only after prompt, timeout, rate-limit, and session-state UX is specified.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across browser SSRF defaults, navigation guard ownership, shared SSRF helpers, and current CDP policy work.
